snippet.title: Value Propositions, Business Models, and Institutional Purpose
snippet.description:
How do value propositions, business models, and institutional purpose fit together—and where do they conflict? This lesson compares investor-owned firms, cooperatives and mutuals, nonprofits, social enterprises, and public-purpose organizations. It treats business frameworks as situated tools, not universal laws, and pays special attention to stakeholder conflict, measurement limits, and proxy failure.

Course: The Modern Firm as an Operational System
Lesson 1: Value Propositions, Business Models, and Institutional Purpose

Selected research sources:
• Strategy Science — Making Sense of Corporate Purpose: https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/stsc.2023.0054
• Harvard Business School — Hybrid organizing and joint social/financial goals: https://www.hbs.edu/ris/download.aspx?name=en_1545043557.pdf
• CEMI — Purpose, identity, and member value in cooperatives and mutuals: https://cemi.com.au/__static/1e2c0ffb62302fe028e9aae46e97b6dc/cemi_dp-1501-_mazzarol_2015.pdf?dl=1
• University of Gloucestershire — Business-model concept and application framework: https://eprints.glos.ac.uk/6442/7/PhD-Thesis%20O%20Stalder_signature_redacted.pdf
• Journal of Political Ecology — Measurement, reporting, and their limits: https://journals.librarypublishing.arizona.edu/jpe/article/8839/galley/9071/view/

This is an AI-assisted visual explainer produced from a bounded source corpus. It is educational material, not legal, accounting, investment, or management advice. Corrections and source challenges are welcome.
